import openpyxl, os, json
p='inputs/sources/fil_01M6JVX0TAVM0VSKFK7F8CCA26.xlsx'
print('exists', os.path.exists(p))
wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=True)

def rows(sheet):
    ws=wb[sheet]
    out=[]
    for r in range(1, ws.max_row+1):
        vals=[ws.cell(row=r,column=c).value for c in range(1, ws.max_column+1)]
        if all(v is None for v in vals): continue
        out.append(vals)
    return out

for s in ['Material','Pack sizes','Batches','Price history']:
    print('SHEET', s, 'max', wb[s].max_row, wb[s].max_column)

mat=rows('Material')
print('material header', mat[0])
print('material first3 repr', [(repr(r[0]), type(r[0]).__name__, repr(r[1])) for r in mat[1:4]])
print('material n', len(mat)-1)

packs=rows('Pack sizes')
print('pack header', packs[0])
print('pack rows', [(repr(r[0]), r[1]) for r in packs[1:]])
print('pack n', len(packs)-1)

bt=rows('Batches')
print('batch header', bt[0])
print('batch first3', [(repr(r[0]), repr(r[1]), repr(r[2]), r[3], repr(r[4])) for r in bt[1:4]])
print('units', sorted(set(str(r[4]).strip().upper() for r in bt[1:])))
print('batch n', len(bt)-1)

pr=rows('Price history')
print('price header', pr[0])
print('price first3 repr', [(repr(r[0]), repr(r[1]), repr(r[2]), repr(r[3]), repr(r[4]), repr(r[5])) for r in pr[1:4]])
print('price n', len(pr)-1)

# selected prices
sel={}
for r in pr[1:]:
    code=str(r[0]); pl=str(r[1]).strip().upper(); cur=str(r[2]).strip().upper()
    vf=str(r[3])[:10]; vt=str(r[4])[:10]; sp=r[5]
    if pl=='RETAIL' and cur=='THB' and vf<='2026-11-03' and vt>='2026-11-03':
        sel.setdefault(code,[]).append(sp)
print('selected price n codes', len(sel), 'multi', {k:v for k,v in sel.items() if len(v)!=1})
print('selected sample', sorted(sel.items())[:5])

# pack lookup
lookup={str(r[0]): r[1] for r in packs[1:]}
agg={}
for code,wh,lot,qty,unit in bt[1:]:
    c=str(code); u=str(unit).strip().upper()
    q=float(qty)
    if u=='CASE': q*=float(lookup[c])
    agg[(c,str(wh))]=agg.get((c,str(wh)),0)+q
print('agg n', len(agg), 'sample', sorted(agg.items())[:8])
print('missing pack codes', sorted(set(str(r[0]) for r in bt[1:]) - set(lookup)))
print('missing price codes', sorted(set(str(r[0]) for r in mat[1:]) - set(sel)))
print('agg codes', len(set(k[0] for k in agg)))
print('inv sample all for one', sorted((k,v) for k,v in agg.items() if k[0]=='000001'))

notes: Price selection on 2026-11-03: each material has four price rows — RETAIL/THB valid 2026-11-01..2026-11-30 (the requested one), RETAIL/THB valid 2026-01-01..2026-10-31 (expired), WHOLESALE/THB valid 2026-01-01..2026-10-31 (expired and wrong price list) and RETAIL/USD valid 2026-11-01..2026-11-30 (wrong currency). Filtering on RETAIL + THB + date yields exactly one row per material, so the wide 2–256 price range is explained by mixture of expired, wholesale and USD rows rather than a data defect; no operator decision is needed for the classification, though the mapping layer must apply the filter rather than take any arbitrary row.

Inventory normalisation: CASE quantities (48 rows) must be multiplied by the material's 'Pieces per CASE' from the Pack sizes sheet (6, 12 or 24, varying by product); PCS quantities (24 rows) are already individual pieces and must be left unchanged. Quantities are then summed per material × warehouse across lots L1–L3, never across warehouses.

Material code is stored/displayed zero-padded ('000001'), so all four sheets must join on it as a string (preserving leading zeros) rather than as a number, otherwise products and their stock/prices cannot be linked.

import openpyxl, os, json
p='inputs/sources/fil_01M6JVX0TAVM0VSKFK7F8CCA26.xlsx'
print('exists', os.path.exists(p))
wb=openpyxl.load_workbook(p, data_only=True)

def rows(sheet):
    ws=wb[sheet]
    out=[]
    for r in range(1, ws.max_row+1):
        vals=[ws.cell(row=r,column=c).value for c in range(1, ws.max_column+1)]
        if all(v is None for v in vals): continue
        out.append(vals)
    return out

for s in ['Material','Pack sizes','Batches','Price history']:
    print('SHEET', s, 'max', wb[s].max_row, wb[s].max_column)

mat=rows('Material')
print('material header', mat[0])
print('material first3 repr', [(repr(r[0]), type(r[0]).__name__, repr(r[1])) for r in mat[1:4]])
print('material n', len(mat)-1)

packs=rows('Pack sizes')
print('pack header', packs[0])
print('pack rows', [(repr(r[0]), r[1]) for r in packs[1:]])
print('pack n', len(packs)-1)

bt=rows('Batches')
print('batch header', bt[0])
print('batch first3', [(repr(r[0]), repr(r[1]), repr(r[2]), r[3], repr(r[4])) for r in bt[1:4]])
print('units', sorted(set(str(r[4]).strip().upper() for r in bt[1:])))
print('batch n', len(bt)-1)

pr=rows('Price history')
print('price header', pr[0])
print('price first3 repr', [(repr(r[0]), repr(r[1]), repr(r[2]), repr(r[3]), repr(r[4]), repr(r[5])) for r in pr[1:4]])
print('price n', len(pr)-1)

# selected prices
sel={}
for r in pr[1:]:
    code=str(r[0]); pl=str(r[1]).strip().upper(); cur=str(r[2]).strip().upper()
    vf=str(r[3])[:10]; vt=str(r[4])[:10]; sp=r[5]
    if pl=='RETAIL' and cur=='THB' and vf<='2026-11-03' and vt>='2026-11-03':
        sel.setdefault(code,[]).append(sp)
print('selected price n codes', len(sel), 'multi', {k:v for k,v in sel.items() if len(v)!=1})
print('selected sample', sorted(sel.items())[:5])

# pack lookup
lookup={str(r[0]): r[1] for r in packs[1:]}
agg={}
for code,wh,lot,qty,unit in bt[1:]:
    c=str(code); u=str(unit).strip().upper()
    q=float(qty)
    if u=='CASE': q*=float(lookup[c])
    agg[(c,str(wh))]=agg.get((c,str(wh)),0)+q
print('agg n', len(agg), 'sample', sorted(agg.items())[:8])
print('missing pack codes', sorted(set(str(r[0]) for r in bt[1:]) - set(lookup)))
print('missing price codes', sorted(set(str(r[0]) for r in mat[1:]) - set(sel)))
print('agg codes', len(set(k[0] for k in agg)))
print('inv sample all for one', sorted((k,v) for k,v in agg.items() if k[0]=='000001'))

verification.scope: Execution and contract checks; business ambiguities require operator answers

notes: Price selection on 2026-11-03: each material has four price rows — RETAIL/THB valid 2026-11-01..2026-11-30 (the requested one), RETAIL/THB valid 2026-01-01..2026-10-31 (expired), WHOLESALE/THB valid 2026-01-01..2026-10-31 (expired and wrong price list) and RETAIL/USD valid 2026-11-01..2026-11-30 (wrong currency). Filtering on RETAIL + THB + date yields exactly one row per material, so the wide 2–256 price range is explained by mixture of expired, wholesale and USD rows rather than a data defect; no operator decision is needed for the classification, though the mapping layer must apply the filter rather than take any arbitrary row.

Inventory normalisation: CASE quantities (48 rows) must be multiplied by the material's 'Pieces per CASE' from the Pack sizes sheet (6, 12 or 24, varying by product); PCS quantities (24 rows) are already individual pieces and must be left unchanged. Quantities are then summed per material × warehouse across lots L1–L3, never across warehouses.

Material code is stored/displayed zero-padded ('000001'), so all four sheets must join on it as a string (preserving leading zeros) rather than as a number, otherwise products and their stock/prices cannot be linked.

tables.reason: 12 rows, one per Material code (unique), each with a human-readable Description; header row on sheet 'Material' — this is the product master list that supplies /sku and /product_name and defines the population of 12 products.

columns.name: Material code

columns.name: Pieces per CASE

columns.name: Material code
